scope: Isolated filesystem, actual SQLite backup API and flock, atomic code/STATE journals, and existing pinned Node; no production install or capacity result.

crashPhaseSubcases.mechanism: fork + os._exit(77), then reload durable journal in parent and recover twice

measuredAssertions: Apply and code rollback retain game DB device/inode, account DB device/inode, release root, game config bytes, dropin bytes and Node bytes.
No release clone, retention cleanup, runtime replacement or accounts-service stop/start occurs.
After health failure, committed game progress 10 -> 20 and a newly inserted account survive automatic code rollback.
Manual code rollback takes a fresh current SQLite backup and preserves committed values 66, 88 and 99.
A dead writer leaves committed value 71 in WAL while immutable main DB still has value 10; the actual SQLite backup API copies value 71.
Injected quick_check failure precedes every code replacement; original R79 code remains intact.
Actual nonblocking flock observes both install.lock and the native daily .backup.lock held during backup; contention reaches no service stop.
A valid nested DB layout with a different native dataRoot, mismatched backup service environment/config, and an environment change during lock wait are refused before service stop.
Native backup binding is checked against manifest dataRoot, backup service Environment, config.database, config SHA and unit-file SHAs.
Startup health failure plus guard ENOSPC or daemon-reload failure still attempts all game/RT stops and preserves the original health exception.
An RT stop error does not skip attempting main-game stop; accounts service remains untouched.
Unknown file hash, changed STATE, changed DB inode, symlink targets and wrong backup identity are refused without overwriting unknown data.
Cleanup failure leaves validated R80 for recover completion; owner policy changes and active admissions are preserved during validated completion.
R80 health requires its version marker and available read-only diagnostics; R79 rollback does not require R80-only fields.
Actual shipped Node v22.23.4, SQLite 3.53.4, node/license SHA, exact bin/node symlink and executable modes validate; no runtime payload is accepted.
fixtureBoundaries: No real systemd daemon, VDS, production HTTP or account authority was accessed.
Systemctl state/commands, central policy RPC, accounts PID/identity and runtime process binding use explicit local fixtures.

Production verify_release invokes the existing Node verifyPackage; fixture tests substitute a full-file SHA/mode verifier and actual r63 core identity. The complete live release package has not been exercised here.
SQLite files are small synthetic databases. Full-size live backup duration, available disk space, Linux service permissions and cold-start health timing remain deployment preflight conditions.
The real pinned Node executable/license and exact current six-file production plan/payload are separately exercised.
These tests establish installer control flow and persistence boundaries, not a server throughput/CPU or player-count forecast.
intentionalSafeStops: Custom backup EnvironmentFile or relevant PassEnvironment/UnsetEnvironment overrides are refused because the stock daily mutex binding cannot be proven.
Manual edits outside known before/after code hashes or changed STATE/config/dropin/DB identity require reconciliation; recover does not overwrite them.
An interrupted SQLite copy with no durable verification metadata is retained in its private attempt directory, never restored or silently deleted; a later attempt may require additional disk space.
If service stop itself fails, every recorded game/RT unit is attempted and the triggering error is preserved; successful OS shutdown cannot be guaranteed by a failed systemctl call.
